difficulty.label: Hard
difficulty.description: Medium to hard. Heavily scenario-based with similar-looking options.

timePressure.label: High
timePressure.description: Many users finish with seconds to spare. Scenario questions take time to analyze.

keyInsights: Only 7-8 straightforward theory questions out of 75 — the rest are scenario-based
Tests 'why' not just 'what' — understanding reasoning is critical
Heavy focus on CMDB Workspace navigation and where to find modules/playbooks
CMDB Health Dashboard KPIs and when to use each
CSDM layers and practical application, not just definitions
commonGotchas: Options look extremely similar — need to understand subtle differences
Navigation questions ask about specific workspace locations
Discovery relationships and data accuracy nuances
CI lifecycle states and when each applies

examPlatform.recommendation: Physical test center strongly recommended over online proctored
onlineIssues: Docker/VM processes can trigger exam pauses
Background services may restart and flag the system

userExperiences.text: The exam is indeed really hard, lots of scenarios and drag and drops. For me what worked is that I did all NowLearning path for CMDB/CSDM with all knowledge checks/labs. Those are really helpful.
I Failed CIS - Data Foundations exam after a long preparation using only ServiceNow Course material. I was not expecting this result, the exam felt very long (it took me the whole 1h30).
The exam imo is really hard, has a lot of scenarios and drag and drops etc. Also a lot about navigating through workspaces and where to find particular modules/playbooks.
Out of 75 I merely got 7-8 straightforward theory-based questions. This is not a theory-only exam. It expects you to think like an implementer, not just someone who has memorized definitions.
Scenario-based questions take time to read, analyze, and eliminate options. I was answering questions until the very last 30 seconds. There was no room to casually review all answers at the end.

prerequisites.note: CIS-DF is now MANDATORY as a prerequisite for CIS-ITSM and other CIS certs as of January 31, 2026

tips: Complete ALL knowledge checks and labs in NowLearning paths — don't skip them
CMDB Health Deep Dive is frequently cited as essential by those who passed
Practice navigating CMDB Workspace in a PDI — know where modules live
Understand the 3 KPIs: Completeness, Compliance, Correctness
For online proctored: disable Docker, VMs, and background dev tools well in advance
Official courses cover ~60-70% — supplement with Health Deep Dive and hands-on practice

difficulty.label: Moderate
difficulty.description: Fundamentally a terminology memorization test, but scenario questions trip people up.

timePressure.label: Moderate
timePressure.description: Most users finish with time to review. Straightforward if prepared.

keyInsights: Table names are tricky — plural vs singular, abbreviations vs full names
Platform navigation questions: 'which tab to do XYZ', button locations
Roles and permissions are heavily scenario-based
CMDB and Service Catalog need extra focus — common weak spots
The 'Additional ServiceNow Fundamentals Content' section is exam gold
commonGotchas: Table name gotchas: task vs tasks, incident vs inc
Similar menu paths with subtle differences
Multi-select questions where options look similar

recommendedResources.name: Udemy CSA Practice Tests
recommendedResources.note: Aim for 90%+ before attempting real exam

userExperiences.text: I was familiar with vocabulary and concepts, but the test was heavily scenario-based... This is where I fell short.
Coming from a web dev background, I struggled with CMDB concepts and CSDM framework. A lot came down to pure memorization which I'm not too happy about.
You have to read the ebook. Video and eBook content are different streams. The e-book is the only thing you need to study to ace this exam.

tips: Complete free developer learning paths BEFORE the paid course
Don't skip the eBook — it contains different content than videos
Pay extra attention to 'Additional ServiceNow Fundamentals Content' section
Use a PDI constantly — look at actual tables, not just slides
Focus extra time on CMDB and Service Catalog
Know your table names precisely — plural/singular matters
